prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour Party Manifesto 2024 — key policies and commitments (summary within 500 words, excluding ideological framing)

Foundations and fiscal rules
- Mission-driven government focused on five goals: sustained G7-leading growth; clean power by 2030; halve serious violent crime and raise confidence in policing; break down barriers to opportunity in education and childcare; build an NHS fit for the future.
- Fiscal rules: current budget to balance; debt falling as a share of GDP by year five; all major fiscal events subject to OBR forecasts.
- No rises in National Insurance, basic/higher/additional rates of Income Tax, or VAT.
- Tax measures: abolish non-dom status; end offshore trust IHT avoidance; close carried interest loophole; modernise HMRC to tackle avoidance.

Security, borders, and defence
- Maintain NATO commitment and the UK’s nuclear deterrent; Strategic Defence Review in year one; path to 2.5% of GDP on defence.
- Counter hostile state threats; implement Martyn’s Law; update counter-extremism rules.
- Create a Border Security Command; end Rwanda scheme; hire more caseworkers; establish a returns unit (+1,000 staff); seek an EU security agreement and additional returns arrangements.

Economy, industry, and infrastructure
- New Industrial Strategy with a statutory Industrial Strategy Council.
- National Wealth Fund (£7.3bn) to crowd in private investment (3:1 target) for ports, gigafactories, steel, CCUS, and green hydrogen.
- Business tax roadmap; cap corporation tax at 25% for the Parliament; retain full expensing; replace business rates in England.
- 10-year infrastructure strategy; National Infrastructure and Service Transformation Authority; planning reform to accelerate nationally significant projects; gigabit broadband and national 5G by 2030.
- Transport: maintain/renew roads; fix 1m potholes annually; restore 2030 ICE phase-out; expand EV charging; bring rail into public ownership as contracts expire; empower mayors to integrate transport; bus franchising and end ban on municipal ownership; support sustainable aviation fuels.
- Innovation: 10-year R&D budgets; Regulatory Innovation Office; AI binding rules for frontier developers; ban sexually explicit deepfakes; National Data Library; support co-ops.

Housing and renting
- Build 1.5m homes in England; restore mandatory targets; fund more planning officers via higher non-UK resident SDLT surcharge.
- Brownfield-first; strategic “grey belt” release under “golden rules”; new towns; stronger cross-boundary planning; reform compulsory purchase.
- Boost social and affordable housing; review Right to Buy discounts; protect new social stock.
- Permanent mortgage guarantee; first-time buyer priority; private renting reform: abolish Section 21, empower rent challenges, extend Awaab’s Law, raise standards; building safety action.

Jobs, pay, and migration
- New Deal for Working People: ban exploitative zero-hours; end fire and rehire; day-one rights to sick pay, parental leave, unfair dismissal protection; Single Enforcement Body.
- Minimum wage remit to reflect cost of living; remove age bands.
- Reform points-based immigration; link shortage visas to domestic training plans; strengthen Migration Advisory Committee.

Education and skills
- 6,500 new teachers in key subjects; free breakfast clubs in all primary schools; 3,000 school-based nurseries.
- Curriculum and assessment review; mental health professionals in every school; Teacher Training Entitlement; reinstate Support Staff Negotiating Body; stronger SEND inclusion.
- Skills England; devolve adult skills; Technical Excellence Colleges; reform Apprenticeship Levy into a flexible Growth and Skills Levy.
- Youth guarantee (18–21): access to training, an apprenticeship, or job support; two weeks’ work experience for every young person.

Crime and justice
- Neighbourhood Policing Guarantee (more officers/PCSOs/specials); procurement/shared services efficiency.
- Respect Orders for antisocial behaviour; specific offence for assaults on shopworkers; tougher shoplifting response.
- Knife crime plan: mandatory interventions; ban zombie-style blades/machetes; Young Futures hubs nationwide; new offence of child criminal exploitation.
- Specialist rape units in every force; fast-track rape courts; stronger vetting and misconduct standards; expanded fraud strategy.
- Build prison places; reduce reoffending via work, housing, and probation reform; Hillsborough Law; address historical injustices.

Clean energy, climate, and nature
- Clean power by 2030: double onshore wind, triple solar, quadruple offshore wind; invest in CCUS, hydrogen, marine; Energy Independence Act.
- Nuclear: extend existing plants; progress Hinkley C/Sizewell C; support SMRs; maintain gas reserve.
- No new North Sea exploration licences; no new coal; fracking ban. Close windfall tax loopholes; extend levy.
- Great British Energy (£8.3bn) to co-invest in clean generation; Local Power Plan.
- Energy market reform; reduce standing charges; upgrade grid.
- British Jobs Bonus (up to £500m/yr) to anchor supply chains; Warm Homes Plan (£6.6bn) to upgrade 5m homes; private rentals to meet efficiency standards by 2030.
- Nature: expand habitats; new National River Walks and forests; stricter water company enforcement and fines.
- Farming: public procurement targets; land-use framework; ELMs reforms; science-led bTB strategy; animal welfare measures.

Health and social care
- Cut waiting lists: 2m extra operations/scans/appointments per year (40,000 weekly); pooled waiting lists; use independent capacity.
- Double CT/MRI scanners; deliver New Hospitals Programme; NHS innovation/adoption strategy; enhance clinical trials; upgraded NHS App.
- Primary care: more GPs; face-to-face option; continuity incentives; pharmacist prescribing; direct referrals; pilot Neighbourhood Health Centres.
- Dentistry Rescue Plan: 700k urgent appointments; reform contract; supervised toothbrushing (ages 3–5).
- National Care Service with national standards; Fair Pay Agreement in adult social care; “home first”; right to family visits.
- Mental health: 8,500 extra staff; Young Futures hubs; modernise Mental Health Act.
- Public health: smoke-free generation; curb youth vaping; restrict junk food ads to children and energy drink sales to under-16s; online and gambling protections; HIV action plan; halve healthy life expectancy gap.

Governance and foreign policy
- Ethics and Integrity Commission; empower Independent Adviser; ban MPs’ paid advisory/consultancy roles; Commons modernisation.
- Lords reforms: remove hereditary peers; retirement at 80; higher standards; consult on replacement second chamber.
- Votes at 16; improve voter registration; fairer voter ID; stronger donation rules.
- Reset with devolved governments; Council of the Nations and Regions.
- Foreign policy: strengthen alliances (US, Europe), no return to EU SM/CU/FOM; targeted trade deals and MRAs; WTO/CPTPP engagement; India/Gulf/Africa partnerships; OECD minimum tax.
- Support for Ukraine; AUKUS; balanced China approach; protect Overseas Territories; Middle East: ceasefire advocacy and recognition of Palestinian state as part of two-state solution.
- Development: rebuild capability; align with foreign policy; restore 0.7% GNI when fiscal conditions allow.

First steps
- Fiscal stability rules; 40,000 extra NHS appointments per week; Border Security Command; Great British Energy; antisocial behaviour crackdown with more neighbourhood police and youth hubs; recruit 6,500 teachers.
